edges.reason: The Owned constructor assigns owner = msg.sender, granting an untrusted caller the privileged onlyOwner role.
onlyOwner modifier checks msg.sender == owner before transferOwnership executes.
onlyOwner modifier gates transfernewun, the blacklist setter, on msg.sender.
onlyOwner modifier gates clearCNDAO, which drains the contract balance.
acceptOwnership requires msg.sender == newOwner to complete the ownership handover.
transfer debits balances[msg.sender] and emits Transfer with msg.sender as from.
approve writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] using the caller as allowance owner.
transferFrom spends allowed[from][msg.sender], tying the caller to the allowance entry.
approveAndCall writes allowed[msg.sender][spender] and passes msg.sender as from into the callback.
clearCNDAO forwards the entire contract balance through _owner.transfer(address(this).balance).
approveAndCall performs an external call to a caller-supplied spender address without a reentrancy guard.
The external call invokes receiveApproval on the attacker-controlled spender contract, handing control back to untrusted code.
Inside receiveApproval the attacker can reenter transferFrom while the freshly granted allowance of approveAndCall is still live.
approveAndCall sets allowed[msg.sender][spender] before the external call, leaving a live allowance during reentrancy.
transfernewun writes the owner-controlled newun blacklist address.
transferFrom silently assigns newun = to when newun == address(0), letting any caller set the blacklist.
transfer requires to != newun, so the owner-set blacklist address blocks transfers.
transferFrom debits balances[from] and credits balances[to].
transfer debits balances[msg.sender] and credits balances[to].
transferFrom decrements allowed[from][msg.sender] by the spent amount.
SafeMath.sub protects the balance and allowance subtractions in transferFrom from underflow.
SafeMath.sub guards the balance debit in transfer so an overdraft reverts.
transfernewun feeds the owner-controlled newun gate used to block transfers.
transfer enforces the newun gate before moving tokens.
transferFrom both enforces and can silently initialize the newun gate.
TokenERC20 constructor sets the fixed _totalSupply value.
TokenERC20 constructor mints the whole supply into balances[owner].
TokenERC20 constructor uses the inherited owner address as the initial token holder.
totalSupply reads _totalSupply when computing the reported supply.
balanceOf reads balances[tokenOwner] from the balances mapping.
Owned constructor directly writes the privileged owner state variable.

normalization_plan.reason: Parameter exists only to carry the staged owner address into the transferOwnership function; it has no independent semantic role.
Parameter exists only as the argument written into newun by transfernewun and should collapse into that function.
Recipient argument of transfer with no standalone meaning outside that function's dataflow.
Amount argument of transfer consumed only by the balance arithmetic inside transfer.
Spender argument used only to key the allowed mapping inside approve.
Allowance amount argument consumed only inside approve.
Source account argument of transferFrom with no role outside that function.
Recipient argument of transferFrom consumed only by its balance and newun logic.
Spend amount argument used only by the subtraction inside transferFrom.
Lookup key parameter of the allowance view function, fully resolved within it.
Second lookup key of allowance, meaningful only inside that function.
Spender parameter is the target of the external call, so it merges into the unsafe external-call operation.
Allowance amount argument consumed only by the allowance write inside approveAndCall.
Arbitrary data parameter is forwarded verbatim into the untrusted receiveApproval call.
Local payable alias of msg.sender exists solely as the destination of the Ether transfer in clearCNDAO.
Query address parameter used only to index balances inside balanceOf.
